title: Whitney's 2-isomorphism theorem for graphings: measurable subtrees on the edges of a weakly 2-connected graphing (Lemma 3.5)
author: Márton Borbényi, Grigory Terlov, László Márton Tóth
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the paper's measurable construction of finite subtrees on the edges of a weakly 2-connected graphing, printed as Lemma 3.5 at source0.tex lines 1185-1193 and delivered with the paper's own complete 85-line proof (lines 1195-1279). The statement is a measurable-combinatorial existence result: for every edge of the graphing one can choose, in a Borel way, a finite subtree that contains that edge, stays inside the unit ball of its cell together with the external vertex boundary, and whose leaves lie in four distinct infinite sides of that ball. The proof is the paper's own assembly over the retained lemmas: it takes the two disjoint paths produced by the retained disjoint-paths lemma, joins them through the edge to connect two distinct sides of the cell, uses the trifurcation structure of the weakly 2-connected graphing to attach two further branches in each endpoint cell, checks that the resulting union is a finite tree contained in the required neighbourhood, and verifies that all four leaves land in distinct infinite sides. This is research-level measurable graph theory about graphings, not a qualifying-examination exercise; the unit is H2.
